findings.title: Queue shutdown uses Python 3.13-only APIs
findings.body: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were introduced in Python 3.13. On earlier supported Python versions, `q.shutdown(...)` raises `AttributeError`, which is swallowed by this broad handler, leaving workers blocked indefinitely in `Queue.get()`. The subsequent joins wait up to five seconds per worker and daemon threads leak; with the default 20 workers this can turn every consumer shutdown into a long hang. Use a portable sentinel/wakeup scheme or explicitly require and enforce a Python version that provides these APIs.

findings.title: The queue pool has no backpressure and can grow without bound
findings.body: Each worker queue is constructed as `queue.Queue()` with its default unbounded capacity, while `submit` always returns immediately. A slow subscription or a hot group therefore accumulates an unlimited number of decoded work items and offset-tracker entries while the Kafka consumer continues polling. This contradicts the stated natural-backpressure guarantee and can exhaust process memory during a sustained slow downstream dependency. Configure a finite queue size and make submission block or otherwise apply an explicit bounded/backpressure policy.

findings.title: Close can process results after the final offset commit
findings.body: `close` signals and joins the commit thread before shutting down the workers. A worker already handling an item can complete it after the commit loop has exited, so its offset is never included in a final commit. On restart Kafka redelivers that successfully handled result, which can duplicate uptime result side effects. Shutdown should stop intake, drain or account for in-flight workers, and perform a final commit after their completions before terminating the commit loop.

findings.title: Negative max-workers silently drops every queued-mode message
findings.body: `--max-workers` accepts negative integers. In queue mode a negative value is truthy, so `FixedQueuePool` creates no queues; every submit then indexes an empty list, is caught by `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, and is marked complete for commit without invoking the result processor. Reject non-positive worker counts (or normalize them consistently) before constructing the pool.
